jtbd: Build the benchmark the arcs-algorethics Decision Firewall was actually designed for, and measure it. Purpose per the originating thread (Perplexity, 2026-09, Rome Call / G7 LAWS ban / Dignitas Infinita): a narrow, provable, fail-closed brake on three one-way-door classes, (1) taking a life / kinetic force, (2) cutting vital care, (3) destroying a livelihood. NOT a general harm classifier. AgentHarm (0/176 both ways, PR #8) was the wrong yardstick for that purpose: its eight categories are out of scope and its tool names are shared by harmful and benign tasks. The real gap is Sister Clare's case from the thread: a patient's oxygen subsidy deprecated with a 200 OK because the action string did not happen to say 'deprecate ... oxygen'. Nobody has measured recall on in-scope cases phrased the way real agent frameworks phrase them. Deliverable: benchmarks/in_scope/ with ~150 hand-built tool calls (tool name + realistic arguments) across the three classes, each with a benign twin (same tool, harmless args), plus scripts/eval_in_scope.py reporting recall per class and benign FPR, committed to benchmarks/history like the others. Expect the first number to be low; that is the honest starting line. Only after that number exists does 'how to raise it' (argument-aware rules per tool, or a YELLOW review band fed by a classifier) become a design question worth asking.
